newsitem.title: USA: Herbert Haft seeks rehearing on Dart control suit.
newsitem.headline: Herbert Haft seeks rehearing on Dart control suit.

text.p: Herbert Haft has asked the Delaware Chancery Court to reconsider a decision Friday that denied him one of his legal options for regaining control of Dart Group Corp, an attorney said Monday.

Haft attorney Elizabeth McGeever told Reuters the rehearing before Chancellor William Allen was requested because of "some errors" in the opinion, but a court date has not yet been scheduled. Chancellor Allen's 12 year term ends in June and he has accepted a teaching position with New York University rather than seek reappointment.
At issue is whether or not Herbert Haft can vote 172,703 shares, or 57 percent of Dart's class B stock, the remainder of which is owned by other factions of the Haft family.

In 1993, during a contentious divorce with his then wife Gloria, Herbert Haft transferred the controlling block of stock to his son Ronald "to avoid the risks of the divorce proceeding" that could have awarded half of his controlling share to his wife, court papers say. But Herbert Haft retained an irrevocable proxy over the shares.

When Herbert and Ronald fell into discord because "the alliance...could not survive the cross pressures of life in the Haft family," Ronald and the Dart board in 1995 negotiated a complex settlement in which Ronald effectively agreed to sell the controlling shares to the corporation, according to Allen's ruling on Friday.
That settlement is being challenged in Herbert's lawsuit.
In a statement Monday, Dart said it hoped the court's ruling "may help it reach a negotiated settlement with Herbert Haft" rather than have to go to trial.

Without a settlement, the Dart Group faces two trials: one with Herbert and one with his former wife Gloria and two of their three children, Robert and Linda. Both suits are in the Chancery Court and both seek control of Dart.

Dart attorney Allen Terrell told Reuters the chairman of the company's executive committee, Larry Schafran, had no comment on Herbert Haft's request for a rehearing and has "referred it to lawyers" who have five days to respond.
Dart is a retail holding company based in Landover, Maryland.
